c.tagline: Fiji's tourism gateway, where beach resorts meet a bustling market town.

taxi.color: varies (often white or silver, with rooftop taxi sign)
taxi.fareNote: Meters exist but many drivers negotiate a flat fare, especially airport-to-resort trips; confirm price before departing.

emergency.note: 917 covers police and ambulance dispatch nationwide; some hotels also keep direct lines to Nadi's Lautoka Hospital or private clinics.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Denarau Island: Port Denarau Marina, Denarau Island, Fiji

avoid.reason: Opportunistic theft around the town and beaches; caution at night

hood_desc: A manicured resort peninsula packed with international beach resorts, a marina, and a golf course; best for honeymooners and families wanting an all-inclusive, self-contained beach holiday.
A laid-back local beach strip with grey-gold sand, budget guesthouses and backpacker hostels; suits travelers wanting a cheap, social, walk-to-the-beach base with sunset views.

Nadi's main tourist strip along Queens Road with the highest density of restaurants, bars, curry houses and mid-range hotels; convenient for travelers without a car who want nightlife and easy transport links.
The compact downtown core with the produce market, handicraft shops, temples and mosques; good for budget travelers wanting an authentic local-city feel and easy bus/onward-travel connections.
A cluster of business-class hotels and a golf course a few minutes from the terminal; ideal for late arrivals/early departures or stopovers who prioritize airport proximity over beach access.
lodging: Radisson Blu Resort Fiji Denarau Island

water.note: Treated municipal water can still carry bacterial contamination; resorts recommend bottled water for visitors.

transit.pay: Local buses are paid in cash to the driver or conductor on boarding (small FJD coins for short hops); there is no citywide tap card. Resort/Denarau shuttle buses and island ferries are usually booked and paid for in advance online or through hotel tour desks.
transit.hours: Local buses run roughly 6am-9pm with reduced evening frequency; no true late-night service, so taxis are the main option after dark.
transit.note: Buses are cheap and frequent along the Queens Road corridor (Airport-Martintar-Nadi Town-Lautoka) but have no fixed published route map; ferries to the Mamanuca/Yasawa islands depart from Port Denarau Marina each morning.

airport.name: Nadi International Airport (NAN)
airport.drive: 15-20 min to Nadi town/Martintar, 30-40 min to Denarau

tip.r: Tipping is not traditional in Fijian culture and not expected, though appreciated at upscale resorts; some hotels add a discretionary service charge to bills.

food.name: Kokoda
food.desc: Fiji's raw fish salad: diced walu cured in lime juice then folded through coconut cream with chilli, onion and tomato, served in a coconut shell.

places.name: Nadina Authentic Fijian Restaurant
places.note: The most focused Fijian kitchen near Nadi; kokoda, palusami and coconut curries with live music some nights.

places.name: Tu's Place
places.note: Long-running local restaurant on the main road serving Fijian plates alongside Indo-Fijian curries.

places.name: The Beach Club Wailoaloa
places.note: Beachfront kitchen with sunset views; kokoda sits on a menu of grills and Fijian specialities.

food.name: Lovo feast
food.desc: Pork, chicken, fish and root vegetables wrapped in banana leaf and buried on hot stones for hours - the ceremonial earth oven of Fijian villages.

places.name: Fiji Culture Village
places.note: Evening cultural show with kava ceremony, meke dancing and a lovo dinner for those not staying at a resort.

places.name: Sofitel Fiji Resort & Spa
places.note: Weekly lovo and meke night open to outside diners; book ahead as it sells out in high season.

places.name: Radisson Blu Resort Fiji
places.note: Regular island-night buffet built around a lovo pit, a reliable option close to Nadi town.

food.name: Fijian fish curry
food.desc: Indo-Fijian curry of reef fish or prawns in a thin, fiercely spiced masala with curry leaves and coconut, eaten with rice or torn roti.

places.name: Zamzam Restaurant
places.note: Local favourite for Fijian-Indian curries; cheap, busy and consistently well reviewed by travellers.

places.name: Raju's
places.note: Budget curry house where most plates come in under FJ$10; go at lunch when the turnover is highest.

places.name: Nadina Authentic Fijian Restaurant
places.note: Fijian-style coconut fish curry in a smarter setting than the town curry shops.

food.name: Roti parcels
food.desc: Soft flatbread wrapped around curried potato, dhal, chicken or goat and tied in paper - Fiji's cheapest and most beloved handheld breakfast and lunch.

places.name: Nadi Market food stalls
places.note: Vendors around the produce market sell roti parcels from early morning for a couple of dollars.

places.name: Zamzam Restaurant
places.note: Takeaway counter turning out roti parcels alongside the sit-down curries.

places.name: Raju's
places.note: Roti and dhal combinations at local prices, popular with airport workers.

food.name: Palusami and rourou
food.desc: Young taro leaves slow-baked in coconut cream, sometimes with corned beef or onion, until they collapse into a rich, silky green stew.

places.name: Nadina Authentic Fijian Restaurant
places.note: Palusami and rourou served as sides with grilled fish or as part of a Fijian tasting plate.

places.name: Sweet Laisa's Kitchen
places.note: Homestyle Fijian staples including rourou, kokoda and ika vakalolo, most dishes around FJ$15.

places.name: Tu's Place
places.note: Everyday Fijian cooking with taro, cassava and coconut greens on the daily menu.

food.name: Ika vakalolo
food.desc: Whole reef fish or walu poached or grilled and finished in coconut milk with ginger and chilli, served with boiled dalo or cassava.

places.name: Nadina Authentic Fijian Restaurant
places.note: Coconut-braised fish alongside garlic mussels and pork belly; the go-to for a full Fijian dinner.

places.name: Sweet Laisa's Kitchen
places.note: Unfussy local kitchen where the coconut fish comes with cassava and greens on one plate.

places.name: The Beach Club Wailoaloa
places.note: Grilled catch of the day with coconut sauce, eaten with your feet nearly in the sand.

food.name: Kava (yaqona)
food.desc: Earthy, peppery infusion of pounded kava root strained through cloth and drunk from a coconut-shell bilo; numbs the lips and is central to Fijian welcome.

places.name: Fiji Culture Village
places.note: Formal sevusevu ceremony explained for visitors, the most respectful first introduction to kava.

places.name: Nadi Market kava stalls
places.note: Upstairs and around the market, vendors sell pounded waka; buy a bundle as a village gift.

places.name: Nadina Authentic Fijian Restaurant
places.note: Kava served with dinner on music nights, a low-key way to try a bilo or two.

food.name: Fiji Gold and fresh bu
food.desc: The islands' easy-drinking lagers, Fiji Gold and Fiji Bitter, and bu - a green drinking coconut machete-opened at the roadside for a few dollars.

places.name: Ed's Bar
places.note: Long-standing expat and local watering hole on the main strip; cheap jugs and late hours.

places.name: The Beach Club Wailoaloa
places.note: Sunset beers and fresh coconuts on the sand, a short taxi from Nadi town.

places.name: Nadi Market and roadside stands
places.note: Green coconuts opened to order; ask them to split it afterwards so you can scoop the flesh.

landmarks: Sri Siva Subramaniya Temple
The largest Hindu temple in the Southern Hemisphere, its vividly painted, sculpture-covered gopuram tower is an unmissable icon of Nadi.
Garden of the Sleeping Giant
A lush orchid garden at the foot of a mountain ridge resembling a sleeping giant, created by actor Raymond Burr.
Sabeto Hot Springs and Mud Pool
Bubbling volcanic mud pools and hot springs set against dramatic hillsides, a favorite for a rejuvenating and photogenic soak.
Denarau Island
Fiji's premier resort island, with palm-lined marinas, white-sand beaches, and postcard sunsets over the water.
Mamanuca Islands
A scattering of dazzling coral-fringed islands just offshore from Nadi, epitomizing the classic South Pacific island paradise.
Nadi Municipal Market
A bustling, colorful market overflowing with tropical produce, spices, and local life at the heart of Nadi town.
Wailoaloa Beach
A relaxed, golden-sand beach near Nadi known for spectacular sunsets over the Mamanuca Islands.
Momi Battery Historical Park
Preserved WWII coastal guns overlooking Momi Bay, offering sweeping ocean views and a glimpse into Fiji's wartime history.
Vuda Marina
A picturesque yacht marina near Nadi, a scenic gateway for sailing trips to the Mamanuca and Yasawa Islands.
Nadi Town and Nadi River
The vibrant commercial hub of western Fiji, where the Nadi River winds past markets, temples, and mangroves.

train.note: Fiji has no passenger railway - the only tracks are private sugar-cane tramways. Travel around Viti Levu by bus, taxi or carrier van.

bus.note: No international buses (Fiji is an island group). Frequent long-distance coaches link Nadi with Suva, Lautoka and the Coral Coast; the main operators are Sunbeam Transport and Pacific Transport, with departures from Nadi bus station where you buy tickets at the counter.

ferry.note: No international ferries. From nearby Port Denarau, South Sea Cruises (https://southseacruisesfiji.com/) runs catamaran transfers to the Mamanuca and Yasawa islands. Larger inter-island ferries to Vanua Levu and Taveuni (e.g. Goundar Shipping) leave from Suva, Natovi and Lautoka, not from Nadi.

half.name: Suva
half.blurb: Fiji's capital, a lively harbor city known as the political and cultural heart of the Pacific.

full.name: Labasa
full.blurb: Fiji's main town on Vanua Levu, known for sugarcane fields and a mix of Fijian and Indo-Fijian culture.
